key_insight: A small emulated quantum component can match or outperform a classical CNN only in some data regimes, but neither architecture is universally best.
engineering_relevance: For medical image classification, the study suggests hybrid quantum-inspired blocks may be useful when data are limited to moderate, but classical CNNs remain stronger at larger scale and are easier to simulate.
method: Compared a hybrid quantum-inspired CNN (HQiCNN) with a parameter-matched classical CNN differing only in one intermediate dense layer.
Evaluated both models on two real medical imaging datasets across multiple hyperparameter settings.
Added SHAP-based explainability metrics (|SHAP|IoU and EMD_pos) to compare where each model focuses.
evidence_signal: Across two datasets and systematic hyperparameter sweeps, HQiCNN performed best in intermediate-data regimes, while the classical CNN achieved top accuracy with the largest training sets.
watch_item: The quantum-inspired components are classically emulated, so performance gains may not translate directly to real quantum hardware and simulation scalability remains a concern.
paper_title: Do emulated quantum circuits change what CNNs look at? Performance and explainability comparison in medical image classification
